items.title: Commerce Ministry Organises Series of Workshops on Opportunities Arising from Free Trade Agreements (FTAs)
items.summary: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Minister, Shri Piyush Goyal, had earlier noted the expanding market access available to Indian businesses through recent Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and urged Indian businesses to utilize the opportunities opened by these agreements.

facts.text: He had said that India's preferential access to global markets, representing around USD 10 trillion in GDP until a few years ago, had expanded by an additional USD 60 trillion over the last four-and-a-half years, taking the total to approximately USD 70 trillion.

With ongoing bilateral and multilateral trade engagements across eight to nine geographies, this was expected to expand to around USD 85 trillion, representing nearly 76 per cent of global GDP, over the next year to year-and-a-half.

Under the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), customs duty on whole cumin seeds has been reduced from 5 per cent to zero, creating opportunities for Rajasthan’s farmers and farmer-producer organisations to expand their presence in the UAE market.
The 5 per cent duty on jewellery has also been removed under the UAE and Australia agreements, while the 2 to 4 per cent duty on jewellery has been removed under the United Kingdom agreement.

items.title: Kamarajar Port Expansion: Strengthening India’s Container Infrastructure
items.summary: 28 NOV 2026 1:49PM by PIB Delhi India's Container Traffic: A Growing Demand for Port Capacity India's maritime network is a vital gateway to global markets. Nearly 95 per cent of the country's trade by volume and around 70 per cent by value moves through maritime routes. As trade grows, ports must expand their capacity to handle larger cargo volumes.

facts.text: Nearly 95 per cent of the country's trade by volume and around 70 per cent by value moves through maritime routes.
Container traffic across Indian ports grew at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.9 per cent between FY 2019–20 and FY 2025–26, reaching 25.7 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs).
Container traffic is projected to reach about 40 million TEUs by FY 2030.
Between FY 2014–15 and FY 2025–26, the cargo-handling capacity of India’s major ports increased from 873 million tonnes per annum to 1,728 million tonnes per annum .
